comparison: Perfect agreement on apoptosis findings (C143-C153). Both recognize that Papss mutants show increased cell death, and critically, both affirm that blocking apoptosis with p35 does not rescue lumen defects, demonstrating independence of these phenotypes. Reviewers explicitly praise this separation as important and well-demonstrated.

Perfect agreement on speculative nature of sulfation substrate claims (C220-C223). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge these as untested hypotheses for future investigation. Reviewers state this limitation 'does not detract from the excellent beginning made here,' accepting the uncertainty as appropriate.

Strong agreement on trafficking defects (C136-C137, C139, C141-C142). Both recognize altered Rab11, Sec15, and Rab7 localization as part of the convincing phenotypic characterization. Reviewers explicitly note these findings as evidence of broad trafficking disruption in Papss mutants.

Strong agreement on rescue experiments (C7-C9, C100). Both emphasize that wild-type Papss rescues the phenotype while catalytically inactive Papss does not, demonstrating that sulfation enzymatic activity is essential. Reviewers explicitly praise the rigorous genetic approach and specificity controls.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C21-C22). Both affirm that the study demonstrates sulfation's requirement for aECM organization during tubulogenesis and that aECM defects cause lumen shaping defects. Reviewers describe the paper as 'important' and the conclusions as well-supported.

Agreement on Crumbs localization defects (C101-C104, C106). OpenEval finds these claims supported by immunostaining and quantification. Peer reviewers acknowledge altered Crb as part of the 'careful phenotypic characterization' using multiple markers, treating the findings as convincing.

Agreement on Golgi defects (C125-C129, C131). OpenEval supports claims about abnormal Golgi arrangement with specificity for Golgi versus ER. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'defects in...Golgi (but not ER) morphology' as part of the convincing characterization, though OpenEval notes some speculation about functional consequences.

Agreement on aECM organization defects (C112-C114, C116-C117). OpenEval finds WGA staining and TEM data showing condensed luminal structures well-supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'defects in both apical and basal ECM organization' as part of the careful phenotypic characterization.

Agreement on temporal dynamics of aECM proteins (C181-C182, C184-C185, C187). OpenEval supports claims about loss of Pio signals at stage 16 and persistence of Dpy signals. Peer reviewers affirm 'Dpy and Pio ZP protein fusions localize abnormally in papss mutants' as part of strong, convincing data.

Agreement on pio mutant phenotype (C188-C190). OpenEval finds constricted lumens and progressive loss of WGA/Dpy signals well-supported. Peer reviewers affirm that 'ZP mutants...have similar SG lumen shaping defects to the papss mutants' and treat this as strong evidence.

Agreement on Np mutant phenotype (C196-C200). OpenEval supports claims about loss of luminal Pio and similar phenotype to pio mutants. Peer reviewers affirm 'Np protease mutants have similar SG lumen shaping defects' and treat the correlation as key evidence.

Agreement on dpy mutant phenotype (C201-C202). OpenEval finds more severe defects and irregular lumens well-supported. Peer reviewers include dpy mutants in their affirmation that 'ZP mutants...have similar SG lumen shaping defects' and treat the data as convincing.

Agreement on Dpy-Pio scaffold model (C214-C215). OpenEval finds these summary conclusions well-supported by collective mutant data. Peer reviewers affirm 'A key conclusion is that SG lumen defects correlate with loss of a Pio+Dpy-dependent filamentous structure' and describe results as strong.

Agreement on mechanical support role (C216-C217). OpenEval notes this is somewhat speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers affirm the overall importance of 'luminal matrix in shaping tubular organs' and treat the mechanical model as part of well-supported conclusions.

Agreement on Np function (C207). OpenEval supports claims about Np's role in Pio cleavage from gain-of-function experiments. Peer reviewers don't explicitly critique these claims and treat Np's role as part of the convincing narrative about ZP protein organization.

Agreement on Pio requirement for Dpy secretion (C194-C195). OpenEval finds this inference well-supported by progressive loss of signals in pio mutants. Peer reviewers treat the dependency relationships as part of the strong evidence for ZP protein interactions.

Agreement on Pio-Dpy filamentous structures (C180). OpenEval supports this inference from colocalization data. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'the involvement of Dpy and Pio in the aECM...and their interactions, are also strong' and describe the data as convincing.

Partial overlap on basic phenotype (C2). OpenEval comprehensively evaluates molecular characterization and thin/irregular lumen phenotype (C1-C2, C69-C76). Peer reviewers focus specifically on rescue experiments but acknowledge the basic phenotype as context.

OpenEval evaluates sulfotyrosine localization and Papss-dependent sulfation (C77-C82) as supported by immunostaining and colocalization data. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though this is foundational evidence for the sulfation mechanism.

OpenEval evaluates quantitative morphological analysis of lumen defects (C83-C91) as supported with adequate sample sizes. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though these measurements underlie the phenotypic characterization praised by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates WGA puncta in Golgi and their reduction in Papss mutants (C118-C124) as supported by colocalization and quantification. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though this relates to the Golgi defects acknowledged by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates Golgi mutant phenotypes (C132-C134) as supported but notes limitations in GM130 data (small sample size, potential selection bias). No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates basal ECM disruption with hemocyte invasion (C154-C159) as supported by hemocyte marker and Nidogen staining. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though basal ECM defects are mentioned by reviewers as part of overall characterization.

OpenEval evaluates Pio as key aECM component (C160-C173) as supported by chitin staining, localization data, and antibody specificity controls. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though Pio findings are acknowledged as part of strong ZP protein data.

OpenEval evaluates Dpy and Qsm localization (C174-C180) as supported, noting caveat about non-functional Dpy-YFP. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though Dpy findings are acknowledged as part of convincing ZP protein characterization.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims from introduction (C23-C68) as supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation needed as these establish context rather than novel findings.
